# opencode-claude-code-acpbridge

**Use [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code) inside [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)**, on your Claude
subscription. Claude Code becomes one more model in OpenCode; Claude does the thinking, and
**OpenCode stays in charge**: it runs the tools, with its own permissions and TUI.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **OpenCode V2 only.**
> - **Requires OpenCode ≥ 2.0.14.** This package uses the V2 plugin runtime: `Plugin.define`,
>   the `plugins[]` config list and the `provider.transform` / `agent.transform` /
>   `session.hook` APIs.
> - **Does not load in OpenCode V1.** For V1, stay on `0.8.x` (see
>   [Upgrading from 0.8.x](#upgrading-from-08x-opencode-v1)).
> - **Tested with:**
>   - OpenCode 2.1.1;
>   - `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.31.x and 0.99.x;
>   - Claude Code CLI 2.1.308.
>
> Check your version with `opencode --version`.

One npm package registers itself both as an OpenCode **plugin** (`default Plugin.define(...)`)
and as a **model provider** (`createACPModelProvider`).

## What is this, in plain words

| Term | What it means here |
| --- | --- |
| **OpenCode** | An open-source coding agent with a TUI, a desktop app and a CLI. They all talk to a local OpenCode **server**. |
| **Plugin** | A package the OpenCode server loads to add features. You list plugins in `opencode.json`, and OpenCode installs them from npm. |
| **Provider / model** | Where OpenCode sends prompts, e.g. `anthropic/claude-…`. This package adds a provider, `acp`, whose models (`acp/default`, `acp/sonnet`, …) are served by Claude Code. |
| **Agent** | A configured assistant in OpenCode (`build`, `plan`, …). This package adds one per Claude Code mode: `claude-default`, `claude-plan`, `claude-acceptedits`, `claude-auto`, `claude-dontask`, `claude-bypasspermissions`. |
| **Tool** | Something the model can call: `read`, `edit`, `bash`, MCP tools… |
| **Claude Code** | Anthropic's coding agent (the `claude` CLI). Running through it keeps usage on your Pro/Max **subscription**. |
| **ACP** | The [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com), a standard way for an editor or client to drive a coding agent. |
| **`claude-agent-acp`** | The ACP adapter for Claude Code (`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`). This package starts it and talks ACP to it. |

### How it works

OpenCode talks to the provider through the Vercel AI SDK `LanguageModelV3` interface. The
provider then:
1. starts `claude-agent-acp`;
2. **turns off Claude Code's own built-in tools**;
3. hands Claude **OpenCode's tools** instead, through a small internal MCP server.

When Claude calls a tool, the provider hands control back to OpenCode. OpenCode runs the tool
(asking for permission if its rules say so) and sends the result back to Claude.

```
OpenCode (orchestrator)                 opencode-claude-code-acpbridge               claude-agent-acp (agent)
  prompt + tools (read, bash, …) ─► doStream ─► ACP session (native tools OFF) ─► Claude reasons
                                               + MCP server with OpenCode's tools ─►
  ◄──── tool-call (read) ─────── finish(tool-calls)  ◄── agent calls read (MCP, deferred)
  runs read (permissions + TUI)
  tool-result ──────────────────► doStream ─► resolves the deferred tools/call ──► agent continues
  ◄──── final text ───────────── finish(stop)        ◄── end_turn
```

- **OpenCode runs the tools**, with its permission system:
  - its own (`read`, `write`, `bash`, `edit`, …);
  - those of the **MCP servers configured in OpenCode**.
- **Claude starts with a "clean brain"**: none of its built-in tools, and none of the skills,
  hooks, agents, plugins or MCP servers in your `~/.claude`. It also gets none of the
  **connectors of your claude.ai account** (Gmail, Drive, …), thanks to `strictMcpConfig`. The
  injected agents switch some native capabilities back on; see
  [Tools and the permission bridge](#tools-and-the-permission-bridge).
- **One persistent Claude Code session per conversation.** After the first turn, only what
  Claude hasn't seen yet is sent, so Claude Code's **prompt cache** is reused instead of
  re-reading the whole history every turn.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| **OpenCode V2 ≥ 2.0.14** | V1 is not supported by this version, see the banner above. |
| **The ACP agent** | `claude-agent-acp`, from `npm i -g @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`, on your `PATH`. The plugin runs whatever you put in `command`; the older names `claude-code-acp` / `@zed-industries/claude-agent-acp` also work. |
| **Claude Code CLI** | `claude` installed and **logged in**: run `claude` once and log in. The provider finds it with `command -v claude`. Set `claudeExecutable` if it isn't on the `PATH`. |
| **Node.js** | The internal MCP server runs with `node`, which must be on the `PATH`. Override it with `ACP_RUNTIME_NODE`. |

You do **not** `npm install` this package yourself: OpenCode installs plugins listed in its
config.

## Install

```bash
# 1. The ACP agent (once)
npm i -g @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp
# 2. Log in to Claude Code if you haven't yet
claude
```

3. Add the plugin to your OpenCode config:
   - global: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`;
   - project: `opencode.json` or `.opencode/opencode.json` at the project root.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "opencode-claude-code-acpbridge", "options": { "command": "claude-agent-acp" } }
  ]
}
```

4. Restart OpenCode: close and reopen the app, or run `opencode service restart`.

On start, the plugin **asks the agent which models it offers**, using a short-lived ACP
connection. It fills in their metadata (context, cost, modalities) from
[models.dev](https://models.dev) and **registers the `acp` provider** at runtime. You'll see
`acp/default`, `acp/sonnet`, `acp/haiku`… in the model picker, and one `claude-<mode>` agent per
Claude Code mode (`claude-default`, `claude-plan`…) in the agent picker. Check from a terminal with `opencode models | grep acp/`.

- **Discovery is cached for 1 hour** in `~/.acp-model-provider/`. Only the first start (or the
  first after the cache expires) pays the 3–5 s it takes to start the agent. Force a refresh
  with `npx opencode-claude-code-acpbridge sync claude-agent-acp`.
- **Metadata** comes from the same catalogue OpenCode uses, `~/.cache/opencode/models.json`,
  falling back to `https://models.dev/api.json`. Costs are informational.
- **Your own provider entry wins.** If you already declare a provider with the same id
  yourself, the plugin leaves it alone.

## Update / reinstall

OpenCode caches installed plugins and **does not refresh them on its own**. In OpenCode 2.1,
`opencode plugin update` only handles TUI plugins, so to move to a new version:

1. Stop OpenCode (close the app, or `opencode service stop`).
2. `rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/npm/opencode-claude-code-acpbridge@*`
3. Start OpenCode again. It installs the latest version.

The first request after that can take a few extra seconds while the package installs.

## First use: agents, models and effort

Pick a **`claude-<mode>`** agent in OpenCode (`claude-default` to start). The `acp/…` models
belong to those agents only: see [Models are paired with the Claude Code agents](#models-are-paired-with-the-claude-code-agents).

**Models.** The list comes from **your account**, not from this package: it's whatever the
agent reports. At the time of writing, on a Max account:

| Model | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `acp/default` | Claude Code's default, recommended model (Opus) |
| `acp/sonnet` | Sonnet |
| `acp/haiku` | Haiku |
| `acp/sonnet[1m]` | Sonnet with a 1M-token context window, labelled "· extra usage": Anthropic bills the 1M window outside the subscription |

- `opus` works through `claudeCode.model` even though discovery doesn't list it.
- You can also use full ids such as `claude-sonnet-4-6`.

**All models and effort levels share one agent process.** The model is applied per session
with `session/set_model` (the `model` config option on claude-agent-acp ≥ 0.99, which dropped
that method), so switching `opus` → `sonnet` mid-conversation keeps the session: no
replay, no new process. The same goes for the agent's mode (`session/set_mode`) and effort.

**Effort** (how hard Claude thinks) is exposed as model **variants**: `acp/sonnet#low` …
`#medium`, `#high`, `#xhigh`, `#max` (V2 syntax `provider/model#variant`). It is applied live
(`setSessionConfigOption`); the model **without** a variant goes back to the session's own
effort. Pick one in the TUI, or set it per agent (see [Agents and subagents](#agents-and-subagents)) or for the whole
provider:

```jsonc
"options": { "command": "claude-agent-acp",
  "claudeCode": { "model": "sonnet", "effort": "xhigh", "thinking": { "type": "enabled", "budgetTokens": 16000 } } }
```

> [!NOTE]
> `opencode run` **without `-m` ignores an agent's `model`**: the V2 CLI uses the global
> model from config. In the CLI pass `-m acp/…`. In the TUI, the agent and model pickers do
> apply the model each agent declares.

## Billing: subscription vs extra usage

In plain ACP the client doesn't control the agent's system prompt. `claude-agent-acp` adds an
extension (`_meta.systemPrompt`) to pass OpenCode's system prompt along. **This matters for
billing:** Anthropic classifies the session by its system prompt. With OpenCode's system prompt
the session counts as a **third-party app** and is billed as **extra usage**; Claude Code's
official preset is billed to your **Pro/Max subscription**.

`claudeCode.systemPromptMode` sets that trade-off:

| Value | Effect | Billing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"preset"` (**default**) | OpenCode's system prompt is **ignored**; Claude uses the official `claude_code` preset. OpenCode's tools are still orchestrated (through MCP); Claude behaves like native Claude Code instead of following OpenCode's instructions. | **Subscription** |
| `"append"` | Preset + OpenCode's system prompt appended: full OpenCode fidelity. | Extra usage |
| `"replace"` | OpenCode's system prompt replaces the preset. | Extra usage |

With `preset`, `forwardEnvContext` (on by default) still passes the **factual** part of
OpenCode's system prompt to Claude as user context, so Claude knows where it is working:
- the `<env>` block: working directory, workspace root, git, platform, date;
- `<available_references>`.

OpenCode's behavioural instructions are never forwarded, so this stays on the subscription.

> Tested empirically:
> - The switch to extra usage comes from an Anthropic classifier that reads the system
>   prompt and recognises a third-party app. The name, the mode or the size don't trigger it.
> - With `preset`, `scripts/verify-billing.mjs` measures **0 extra usage**, including with
>   the native features the injected agents enable.

Everything goes in the plugin's `options`. Options not specific to the plugin are passed on to

## Status and limitations

| Status | Feature |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ | Streaming chat, with Claude's **reasoning block** shown in OpenCode (summarized thinking by default). |
| ✅ | **Native capabilities plus permission bridge**: skills, subagents, MCP resource search and project memory, each native action approved through OpenCode's `question` dialog. All on the **subscription** (verified). |
| ✅ | **Clean-brain mode** (`mode: "bypassPermissions"`, no native toggles): no native tools, no claude.ai connectors, only OpenCode's tools. |
| ✅ | **Auto-registration** with models.dev metadata, refreshable with `npx opencode-claude-code-acpbridge sync`. |
| ✅ | **Persistent session per conversation** (prompt cache), **resume across restarts**, several conversations and subagents at once on one agent process, idle sessions closed automatically. |
| ✅ | **Token usage**: OpenCode sees the **real** context size, including on tool steps. |
| ✅ | **Model switching mid-session** in both directions (`acp` ↔ other providers) without losing context. |
| ℹ️ | Which models answer depends on your account. On a Max account (June 2026): `default` (Opus), `sonnet`, `sonnet[1m]`, `haiku`, plus `opus` though it isn't listed. |
| 🔜 | `historyMode: "v2"` as the default, once validated in real use (shadow mode). |

## Upgrading from 0.8.x (OpenCode V1)

1. **Plugin config**: `"plugin": [[pkg, {opts}]]` → `"plugins": [{ "package": pkg, "options": {…} }]`. If you
   declared `provider.acp` by hand, remove it: the plugin registers it at runtime.
2. **Agents**:
   - the `agent:` section becomes `agents:`;
   - `permission` (a map) becomes `permissions` (a ruleset: `[{ "action": "bash", "resource": "git *", "effect": "allow" }]`);
   - `disable` becomes `disabled`.
3. **Variants**: `acp/opus:low` → `acp/opus#low` (V2 syntax `provider/model#variant`).
4. **Per-agent options** (mode, effort, native toggles): from `agent.<n>.options` to
   `plugins[0].options.agents.<n>.options`.
5. **`claude_permission` is gone.** The permission bridge now uses OpenCode's `question` tool.
   Move any bridge rules to `agents.<n>.permissions`; the bridge evaluates them fail-closed.
6. **Local development**: point `package` at the repository **directory**, which has a root
   `index.js` re-exporting `dist/`. Don't point it at a file. Build with `npm run build`.
7. **CLI**: `opencode run` without `-m` ignores `agent.model`, so use `opencode run -m acp/…`.

## Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aorizondo/opencode-claude-code-acpbridge.git
cd opencode-claude-code-acpbridge
npm install
npm run build          # → dist/
npm test               # tsc + node --test
```

- **Unit tests** (`npm test`) need no external services. An in-process fake ACP agent
  (`test/fake-agent.mjs`: real ACP, plus real MCP against `mcp-runtime.js`) covers each
  behaviour and each fixed bug. The prompts in `test/fixtures/v2/` are **real** OpenCode V2
  prompts recorded with `ACP_RECORD`.
- **Against the real agent**: `VERIFY_MODEL=haiku node scripts/verify-<name>.mjs`. Scripts:
  - `verify-session-continuity`;
  - `verify-smart-revert`;
  - `verify-interleave-fix`;
  - `verify-stream-integrity`;
  - `verify-billing`.
- **Run your checkout in OpenCode**: point the plugin at the repository directory,
  `"plugins": [{ "package": "/path/to/opencode-claude-code-acpbridge", "options": { "command": "claude-agent-acp" } }]`.
  OpenCode loads `<dir>/index.*`, and the root `index.js` re-exports `dist/`, so build first.
- **Smoke test**: `opencode run --standalone --agent claude-default -m acp/default "…"` in a test
  project. The bridge's `question` dialog needs the interactive TUI.
- The package also exports `createACPProviderFromEnv`. It is the upstream
  `@mcpc-tech/acp-ai-provider` without tool orchestration, if you only want plain chat.

# Configuration examples

Ready-made `opencode.json` files for common use cases. **OpenCode V2 only**: these use the V2
config format (`"plugins": [{ "package", "options" }]`, `"agents"`, `"providers"`) and don't work
with OpenCode V1.

Copy the one that fits into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (applies to every project) or
into `opencode.json` at the root of a project. Merge it with what you already have.

> **Local development** (without the npm package): replace
> `"package": "opencode-claude-code-acpbridge"` with the **directory** of your checkout, e.g.
> `"package": "/path/to/opencode-claude-code-acpbridge"`. OpenCode V2 rejects a file as a plugin
> target. The directory needs the root `index.js`, which re-exports `dist/`, so build it first
> with `npm run build`. Everything else stays the same.

| File | Use case | Key settings |

## [0.10.0] — 2026-10-22 — history sync, concurrency and continuity across models

A full review of the bridge against the OpenCode V2 source, `claude-agent-acp` 0.31 and
**real** recorded sessions. The goal: switch between `acp` and other models in the same
session without losing anything, and reuse the Claude Code session whenever possible.
Everything below is covered by `npm test` (a fake ACP agent plus real V2 prompts) and by the
scripts that run against the real agent.

### Fixed

- **Claude's own reply was resent every turn** as `"Assistant: …"` inside the user message
  (seen in transcripts; the model once called it "a fake message"). The provider now
  recognises its own output (emitted texts, ids carrying its prefix) and does not send it back.
- **Lost messages**: what you typed while the agent was working (a *steer*), and the message
  sent after **interrupting** a tool, were treated as a continuation of the turn and never
  arrived. Now a steer joins the running turn (Claude Code's native queue), and an
  interruption cancels the turn before the new message is sent.
- **Turns by another model attributed to Claude**: they arrived as
  `Assistant: [Called tool …]`, so Claude believed it had made them. They now come wrapped in
  `<other_model_turn>`.
- **Concurrent tool calls dropped** (native subagents running in parallel): the second call
  was lost and the turn hung. Calls are now queued; read-only ones (`readOnlyHint`) are batched
  into one step that OpenCode runs in parallel.
- **Security**: the bridge's `perm_N` ids repeated across processes, so an old answer
  ("Always allow") could approve a new permission. Ids now carry their own prefix and the last
  match wins.
- An old prompt finishing (cancelled or merged) closed the stream of the following turn; text
  from an aborted turn showed up at the start of the next one.
- Two simultaneous calls for the same conversation created two sessions (one orphaned).
- **Usage**: `PromptResponse.usage` is the sum of every request in the turn; reporting it as a
  single request inflated the context size and triggered early compactions. The real context
  occupancy (`usage_update.used`) is reported now, also on tool steps.
- **Sessions were never closed**: each one left a `claude` process running. Now
  `session/close` is sent when a session is discarded, with an idle TTL (15 min; subagents
  2 min) and an LRU of 6.
- **Junk titles** (`<invoke name="Read">`): with `preset`, the title instructions never reached
  Claude. The plugin now titles the session from its first message, without calling the model.
- **OpenCode subagents running on `acp`** (they inherit the parent's model): with no profile,
  every OpenCode tool asked the bridge for permission, and `general` (which has no `question`
  tool) got them denied. Now every agent auto-allows OpenCode's tools, and the bridge denies
  with a reason when the agent cannot ask. Rules are published for every agent.
- Switching to an agent with a different native profile reused the session with the old
  profile; it now **forks** it (`session/fork`), keeping the context.
- Going back from plan to `claude-code` downgraded to `default` the mode chosen when the plan
  was approved.
- Resume after a restart resent the provider's own traffic, and happened even when the
  registry entry belonged to another conversation; the registry is now also updated mid-turn.
- A session lost on the agent side (dead `claude` process) failed on every turn; it is now
  dropped and resumed.
- `mcp-runtime` ignored SIGTERM (registering the handler disables the default exit).

### Added

- **Native compaction**: `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=75` (`autoCompactPct`) makes Claude
  compact before OpenCode does; if OpenCode compacts, the summary comes from the **live
  session** (before: a full cold replay, 17K+ characters in the recording).
- **`historyMode`** (default `shadow`): a fingerprint made of anchors (user messages + tool ids)
  that is immune to V2 re-rendering (reasoning→text, model switches), transient plan reminders
  and DCP tags. In `shadow` it only logs disagreements; `v2` decides, and also adopts
  OpenCode's checkpoint or catches up with another model's.
- **`smartRevert`** (on by default): a revert forks the session right before the reverted
  message (`resumeSessionAt`) instead of replaying; `false` turns it off.
- **One agent process for every model** of the provider; switching models uses
  `session/set_model` without losing the session.
- **Portable native activity** (`nativeActivity`): Task/WebSearch/Skill leave a `⚙ …` line
  (with its result) in the reply, so any model can see it.
- **ExitPlanMode** with the real options (auto / accept edits / approve each edit / keep
  planning); a typed answer comes back as feedback.
- Claude usage limit → a clear, non-retryable error ("switch models").
- Bounded (~400K characters) and labelled replay; the current request is sent separately.
- V2's initial **Code Mode** catalog is forwarded as context.
- Log file under `~/.acp-model-provider/logs/`, the `ACP_RECORD` recorder,
  `scripts/sanitize-recording.mjs`, the `npm test` suite, `scripts/verify-smart-revert.mjs`.
- Options: `historyMode`, `catchupResultChars`, `parallelTools`, `toolBatchMs`,
  `autoCompactPct`, `nativeActivity(Chars)`, `maxLiveSessions`, `idle/childSessionTtlMs`,
  `smartRevert`; plugin: `titleFromModel`.

### Changed

- Native `Read` is no longer in the default profile (what it read never reached OpenCode's
  history); V2's `read` covers images and PDFs.
- `allowedTools` defaults to `["mcp__opencode"]` for every agent.
- The `claude-code*` agents deny `compress` (opencode-dcp).
- The session registry has an in-memory cache and pruning (30 days / 500 entries).

## [0.8.0] — 2026-08-21

A release focused on **token cost** and **session continuity**. Almost every problem had the
same root cause: the provider recreated the ACP session far too easily, and each recreation
means a full history replay and a cold prompt cache. Now a conversation survives changes of
agent, tools and system prompt while keeping the same Claude Code session.

### ⚠️ Breaking

- **`claudeCode.configDir` now inherits `~/.claude` by default** (previously `"isolated"`).
  Sessions started from OpenCode are now stored in `~/.claude/projects/…`, so **they can be
  resumed natively with `claude --resume <id>`** (the provider prints the id when it creates
  each session). This does **not** bring back the user's ecosystem: `settingSources`, `tools`
  and `strictMcpConfig` still decide what the agent loads; `configDir` only decides where its
  state lives. To get the old behaviour back: `"configDir": "isolated"`. A welcome side effect:
  the credentials symlink is gone, and with it the class of 401 desync bugs.
- **The advertised context limit is no longer inflated to 1M** for the `default` model; only
  the real `[1m]` variants declare it. Advertising 1M kept OpenCode's auto-compaction from ever
  triggering, and the conversation grew without bound.

### Fixed

- **Disproportionate token spend (the main cause).** `sentLen` was set at the start of the
  turn and not updated in the continuation branch, so every turn resent as plain text **all the
  `tool-call`/`tool-result` pairs of the previous turn** (full file dumps, shell output, greps)
  that the agent **already had** in its session. It also invalidated the prompt cache every
  turn. The state now records the fingerprint of the history already sent, and the provider's
  own calls (identified by the host's nonce prefix) are left out of the catch-up; other
  models' results are truncated to 2000 characters.
- **Switching agents destroyed the session and replayed everything.** `systemKey` hashed
  OpenCode's system prompt even with `systemPromptMode: "preset"`, a mode in which that system
  prompt is **never sent to the agent**. Any agent switch, or the churn of OpenCode's dynamic
  blocks (date, `AGENTS.md`, skills), recreated the session over text the agent never saw.
  The system prompt now counts as identity only when it is actually sent, and the
  `claude-code-plan` → build → `claude-code` flow keeps the same ACP session.
- **A change in the tool set no longer recreates the session.** It is applied live to the
  running session through `notifications/tools/list_changed` over the MCP channel.
- **The title/summary model call no longer destroyed the conversation.** It arrives with
  `tools=0` on the same model and session; it is now served by a separate throwaway session.
- **Truncated text and invisible reasoning (same cause).** Text and thinking arrive over ACP
  stdio, while tool calls arrive over the `McpHost` TCP socket, with no guaranteed ordering.
  When a tool call closed the stream, everything still arriving was **silently dropped**, and
  since thinking is emitted right before each tool call, it vanished almost entirely even with
  `effort: max`. Those chunks are now **buffered** and flushed in order into the continuation
  stream.
- **Reverting messages left both sides out of sync.** The provider kept only a counter, so a
  truncated history fell into a silent fallback that resent **the whole** history on top of a
  session that already had it. The history fingerprint is now compared to tell an *append*
  (send only what's new) from a *revert* / *compaction divergence* (new session from the
  truncated history). The plugin also listens to `session.updated` and drops the registered
  link as soon as the revert point moves.
- **Two simultaneous conversations destroyed each other's session.** There was a single
  `TurnState` per model instance, shared by every chat and subagent: each turn switched
  conversation and forced a full replay. There is now **one session per conversation** (with an
  LRU bound), and the agent's callbacks are routed by `sessionId`.
- **`claude-code-plan` had no way out of plan mode.** `ExitPlanMode` was not exposed to the
  agent, it did not see OpenCode's `plan_exit`, and the bridge forced `plan` again every turn:
  a closed loop that left all the already-written `switch_mode` handling dead. `ExitPlanMode`
  is now exposed, and **re-selecting the plan agent by hand re-applies `mode: "plan"`**
  (before, `modeChangedByAgent` was never reset).
- **Approving a plan granted `bypassPermissions`.** The first `allow_*` option offered by the
  agent was picked, and that is the broadest one. `default` (manual approval of edits) is now
  preferred for `switch_mode`.
- **The agent did not use OpenCode's `question` tool.** Its instruction lives in OpenCode's
  system prompt, which is not forwarded with `preset`, and its native `AskUserQuestion` is
  disabled by the ACP agent itself. The `question` tool's **description** now says so
  explicitly (a tool description is not a system prompt: it doesn't affect billing).
- **The agent had no web search.** OpenCode only registers its `websearch` for
  `providerID: "opencode"` (or with exa/parallel), and native `WebSearch` was in
  `disallowedTools`. Native `WebSearch` is now part of the profile.
- **Tool results arrived flattened to text**, losing images and attachments. Structured
  content is now mapped to MCP blocks.
- **A rejected `effort` was silently swallowed**; a warning is now printed to stderr.
- **Cancelling a turn no longer tears down the session**: the turn is cancelled and the session
  (and its cache) is kept for the next message.

### Changed

- **`claude-code` and `claude-code-plan` share exactly the same tool and permission profile**,
  and differ **only** in their initial mode. Before, they also differed in `nativeTools`, which
  left a half-way state: the agent left plan mode on its own (OpenCode does not switch agents
  because of it) and believed it could edit while OpenCode still gave it the restricted
  profile.
- **New option `claudeCode.forwardEnvContext`** (default `true`): forwards the **factual** part
  of OpenCode's system prompt (`<env>`: working directory, workspace root, git, platform, date;
  and `<available_references>`) as user context. With `preset` the system prompt never reaches
  the agent, so it worked without knowing where it was. Only factual blocks are sent, never
  OpenCode's behavioural instructions, so the session stays on the subscription (verified with
  `scripts/verify-billing.mjs`). It is sent in full once per session, then only the delta of
  what changed.
- The Claude Code session id is logged to stderr when the session is created, without needing
  `ACP_DEBUG`, together with the command to resume it.

### Known issues

- The per-turn `usage` breakdown is reported cumulatively by the ACP agent, and some turns may
  show a delta of 0; the session total is correct.

## Changes between 0.7.0 and 0.8.0

These entries were listed as "Unreleased" after 0.7.0 and shipped with 0.8.0.

### Added

- **Proper `ExitPlanMode` handling.** When the agent leaves plan mode (it arrives as a
  `requestPermission` with `toolCall.kind === "switch_mode"`):
  - the **plan** (markdown in `rawInput.plan`) is now **rendered as assistant text** before the
    approval prompt, instead of being buried in the metadata;
  - the permission is labelled consistently as **`ExitPlanMode`** (a
    `permission: { ExitPlanMode: "allow" }` rule is possible; by default it asks);
  - `current_mode_update` is now handled and, once the plan is approved (plan →
    default/acceptEdits), the bridge **stops forcing** the agent's mode again, so the
    implementation continues in the same session instead of going back to plan on the next
    turn.

### Fixed

- **Switching from a normal agent to `claude-code` (ACP) mid-session ignored all previous
  progress.** Both the live reuse of an ACP session (`this.current`, which survives an agent
  switch intact) and the `resume` after a process restart assumed that the only new thing
  since the last ACP turn was the latest user message (`lastUserBlocks`). If another agent
  (e.g. a different model) ran turns in the same OpenCode conversation in between, those turns
  never reached Claude Code: it resumed/reused with its old history plus only the newest
  message, which looked like a fresh session. `TurnState` now keeps `sentLen` (how far the
  agent's knowledge goes), and each send uses `catchUpBlocks`, which rebuilds as a transcript
  (with role prefixes) **everything** that happened from `sentLen` on: one message in the
  normal case, the whole stretch if another agent ran in between.
- **Corrupted tool results (stale/misrouted results).** The `toolCallId` was minted as
  `acp_${counter}` with a counter **per `McpHost`** that **reset to 0** on every ACP session
  reset (tool/system prompt change, new conversation, resume). Within one conversation
  OpenCode resends the whole history; after a reset a new call got `acp_1` again, and
  `detectContinuation` matched it with an **old** tool result in the history: glob returned a
  README, bash returned "background agent task launched", and so on. Each host now uses a
  **random nonce prefix** (`acp_<hex>_${counter}`), so ids never collide across sessions,
  process restarts or resumes.
- **`claude-code-plan`: subagents (`Task`) failed.** The plan agent had no `nativeSubagents`,
  so its `Task` was not Claude Code's native one but OpenCode's forwarded `task`. OpenCode then
  created subagents (`explore`, …) routed to **other providers** (`opencode-go`/`opencode`),
  which failed with *Bad Gateway* / *Insufficient Balance* / *ProviderModelNotFound*.
  `claude-code-plan` now shares the same native feature base as `claude-code` (native
  subagents that run on the subscription and delegate tools to OpenCode), with `mode: "plan"`

# Development — `opencode-claude-code-acpbridge`

How the package works inside, its key flows, and how to extend it. For usage see the
[README](../README.md); for ready-made configs see [examples/](../examples/).

> **OpenCode V2 only.** The plugin half uses the V2 plugin runtime (`Plugin.define`, promise
> API) and the V2 config format. It does not load in OpenCode V1.

---

## 1. Overview

One npm package that OpenCode loads as **two things at once**:

- **Provider** (`createACPModelProvider`): implements `LanguageModelV3` from the Vercel AI
  SDK. Underneath it is an **ACP client** (Agent Client Protocol) that spawns
  `claude-agent-acp`, the ACP adapter for Claude Code.
- **Plugin** (`export default Plugin.define({ id, setup })`, V2 promise API):
  - registers the provider and the agents through transforms;
  - injects the session id and the per-call options through the `context` hook;
  - names sessions without a model call (`title` hook);
  - drops the stored session link on `session.revert.*` events.

  For local development the entry point is the root `index.js`: when the plugin target is a
  directory, OpenCode's `Host.resolve` looks for `<dir>/index.*`.

The guiding principle is **"OpenCode orchestrates"**. Claude only **reasons and proposes**
tool calls; **OpenCode runs them** (with its permissions and TUI) and feeds the result back.
To get there, Claude Code's common native tools are **disabled**, and **OpenCode's tools** are
exposed to it through a synthetic MCP server. The native tools that stay enabled are the ones
with no OpenCode equivalent, and they go through the **permission bridge** (§4).

---

## 2. Architecture

```
                 ┌───────────────────────── OpenCode process ──────────────────────────┐
                 │                                                                      │
 OpenCode  ──────┼─►  Plugin (V2)                    Provider (LanguageModelV3)          │
  (TUI/run)      │      • provider.transform:           • doStream(prompt, tools)        │
                 │      • registers the acp provider    • ACPOrchestratorModel           │
                 │      • agent.transform:              persistent ACP session           │
                 │          claude-<mode> + rules ────► providerOptions.acp              │
                 │      • session.hook("context"): ◄─── ocSession/ocAgent/resume*        │
                 │          session id + options ─────► + per-agent mode/effort          │
                 │      • event: session.revert.* → clearLink                            │
                 │                                       │                               │
                 │                               McpHost (TCP) ◄── OpenCode's tools      │
                 │                                         │ getServerConfig()           │
                 └─────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┘
                                                           │ spawn (stdio JSON-RPC, ACP)
                                                           ▼
                                             claude-agent-acp (separate process)
                                                           │  spawns over stdio
                                                           ▼
                                             mcp-runtime.js (node) ──TCP──► McpHost
                                             (MCP server "opencode", defers tools/call)
```

- **ACP channel:** stdio between the provider and `claude-agent-acp` (newline-delimited
  JSON-RPC, `@agentclientprotocol/sdk`).
- **Tool channel:** the agent starts `mcp-runtime.js` as an MCP server over stdio. The runtime
  forwards each `tools/call` over **TCP** to the `McpHost` inside the provider, which
  **defers** it until OpenCode has run the tool.

## 3. Components (`src/`)

### `provider/model.ts` — `ACPOrchestratorModel`
The core. Implements `doStream`/`doGenerate` and keeps **one persistent ACP session per
conversation**.

- **Connection** (`connect`): spawns the agent with its environment and opens a
  `ClientSideConnection`, then `initialize`. The environment it sets:
  - `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE`;
  - `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, only with `configDir: "isolated"` or a path;
  - `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` (`autoCompactPct`, default 75);
  - `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, only when `claudeCode.model` is set;
  - `CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT`, only with `streamCloseTimeoutMs`. claude-agent-acp
    0.31 doesn't read it.

  `requestPermission` is **not** auto-approved: it goes through the permission bridge (§4).
- **Session identity:** one `TurnState` per conversation, in a `Map` keyed by the OpenCode
  session id, plus an index by ACP `sessionId` to route the agent's callbacks. Recreating a
  session throws away Claude's prompt cache, which lives and dies with it, so it is recreated
  as rarely as possible:
  - `systemKey` only counts **if the system prompt actually travels**. With
    `systemPromptMode: "preset"` (the default) it doesn't, so switching agents in OpenCode
    recreates nothing.
  - `toolsKey` doesn't recreate either: a different tool set is applied live with an MCP
    `notifications/tools/list_changed`.
  - `cfgKey` is the full **creation profile**: `buildClaudeCodeOptions` without model and
    effort, plus `systemPromptMode`. When it changes (an agent with other native tools), the
    session is **forked** (`unstable_forkSession` with the new `_meta`, `forkInPlace`) instead
    of recreated.
  - A different acp model is applied with `unstable_setSessionModel`. There is **one**
    orchestrator (one agent process) for every model of the provider; each model id is an
    `ACPModelView` over it (`factory.ts`).
  - A call without tools (titles or summaries in programmatic use) goes to a separate
    `:notools` session that closes after answering. Inside OpenCode the plugin sets titles
    without a model.
  - A per-conversation lock (`withLock`) guards creating and reusing a session.
- **History sync** (`history.ts`): two fingerprints of what the agent already knows.
  - `sentKeys`: the legacy per-message keys.
  - `sentAnchors`: the user's messages plus tool-call ids.
  - `historyMode` decides which one acts; `shadow` logs every disagreement.
  - The incoming prompt is classified as *append* (send only the tail), *revert* or
    *divergence*.
  - The tail is cleaned of the agent's **own output** (`dropOwnLead`: emitted texts in
    `ownTexts`, ids with its own prefix in `ownPrefixes`).
  - Another model's turns travel as `<other_model_turn>`. A full replay is a bounded
    `<conversation_history>` (about 400,000 characters, newest kept).
- **Turns and generations:** each `session/prompt` carries a generation (`sendPrompt`). The
  completion of an old one, cancelled or merged by the agent's prompt queue, is ignored.
  `abortTurn` cancels, rejects the deferred MCP calls and drains pending permissions; `settle`
  waits for the old prompt to finish.
- **Stream buffer** (`emit`/`flushPending`): text and thinking arrive over the ACP stdio,
  while tool calls arrive over the host's TCP socket, with no guaranteed order. When a tool
  call closes the stream, whatever keeps arriving is **buffered** and flushed into the
  continuation stream instead of being lost.
- **Factual context** (`contextBlocks`): with `preset`, OpenCode's system prompt never reaches
  the agent. So its `<env>` block (and `<available_references>`) is forwarded as **user**
  content: in full the first time, then only the changes.
- **`effectiveCtrl(options)`**: merges `config.claudeCode` with `providerOptions.acp`
  (per-agent or per-call mode, effort, thinking, systemPromptMode and the native toggles).
- **`applySessionConfig`**: applies the model (`unstable_setSessionModel`), the `mode`
  (`setSessionMode`) and the `effort` (`setSessionConfigOption`) **live**, without
  recreating the session.
- **Deferred tool flow:** see §4.
- **Usage** (`usageNow`): the context size comes from `usage_update.used`, the last request.
  `PromptResponse.usage` is the SUM over the turn and only provides the cache proportions.
- **Compaction:**
  - `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` makes Claude Code compact its own session first.
  - A compaction request from OpenCode (`requestKind`) is served in the live session
    (`serveCompaction`).
  - With `historyMode: "v2"`, a hidden native `/compact` follows (`nativeCompact`) and the
    checkpoint is adopted with no new session.
- **Resources:**
  - `session/close` (through `extMethod`) when a session is dropped;
  - idle sweep (`sweepIdle`) with per-session and per-subagent TTLs;
  - an LRU cap of `maxLiveSessions` (default 6).

### `acp/mcp-host.ts` — `McpHost`
TCP server inside the provider. `setTools()` receives OpenCode's tools; it answers the
runtime's `getTools`/`callTool`. It **defers** each `callTool`: it keeps
`{socket, runtimeId}` per `toolCallId` and answers when OpenCode delivers the result
(`resolveToolCall`), or fails it (`rejectToolCall`).

### `acp/mcp-runtime.ts`
**Dependency-free** stdio MCP server (only `node:net`/`node:readline`) that the agent spawns.
It forwards `tools/list`/`tools/call` over TCP to the host (port in `ACP_TOOL_HOST_PORT`).
- **No client-side timeout:** a `tools/call` can wait for OpenCode as long as the agent allows
  (`MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, about 27 h in claude-agent-acp 0.31).
- **Forwarding:** `_meta["claudecode/toolUseId"]` and the agent's `notifications/cancelled` go
  on to the host.
- **Shutdown:** it is hardened against `EPIPE`/`ECONNRESET`, which happen when the agent kills
  it on close.

`ClaudeCodeControl` (the options type), `buildClaudeCodeOptions` (builds

- **"Clean brain" by default:**
  - `tools: []`, `settingSources: []`;

  - `session.revert.committed|cleared` → `clearLink`, so a restart never resumes a session

  - `session.created|agent.selected|model.selected` → pairing watcher. The TUI commits a

  `tool execute.before` can.

## 4. Key flows

### Deferred tool call (the core of "OpenCode orchestrates")
1. `doStream` receives the prompt and the tools. The provider exposes the tools through
   `McpHost` and sends the prompt to the agent.
2. The agent decides to use a tool and calls the `mcp-runtime` MCP server, which forwards
   `callTool` over TCP to the `McpHost`.
3. `McpHost.onToolCall` → the provider **emits to OpenCode**
   `tool-input-start/delta/end` → `tool-call` (with the **real** tool name) →
   `finish("tool-calls")`, and **leaves the MCP `callTool` pending**.
4. OpenCode runs the tool (permissions, TUI) and brings the `tool-result` in the **next**
   `doStream`.
5. The provider detects the continuation (`detectContinuation`) and calls
   `McpHost.resolveToolCall(id, result)`. The MCP `callTool` finally answers and the agent
   continues the same turn.

Details:
- **Grouping by step.** Tool calls are grouped per step (`addStepItem`/`closeStep`). Read-only
  ones wait `toolBatchMs` for their siblings, and all of them leave with a **single** `finish`.
- **Late calls.** Calls that arrive once the stream has closed are queued (`queuedItems`) and
  leave at the start of the next continuation.
- **Messages after the results.** If the continuation brings messages after the tool results
  (a steer, a `<system-update>`, a subagent result, the max-steps prefill), they go into the
  running turn: as a queued prompt, or appended to the last result when the agent doesn't
  support `promptQueueing`.
- **Aborts.** If a result is `aborted` and a new message follows, the old turn is cancelled and
  the message goes as a new turn.
- **Cancelled calls.** An agent `notifications/cancelled` withdraws a call that hasn't been
  emitted yet.

### Sessions: incremental messages (the central requirement)
ACP is a live session: the agent remembers everything already sent. So **re-sending the
whole history every turn burns tokens and breaks the prompt cache** (commit `4a7d7be`, 0.8.0).
OpenCode, on the other hand, always builds the full prompt. The provider decides what actually
travels:

- **Reuse** (same process, same conversation): the fingerprints detect an *append* and only
  the **tail** is sent, without the agent's own output. Nothing is re-sent and the cache stays
  warm. Turns by another model (after a model switch) travel as `<other_model_turn>`.
- **Resume** (new process): the `context` hook brings `resumeId`/`resumeLen` from the
  `sessions.json` registry. If the history grew without diverging and the conversation key
  matches, `unstable_resumeSession(acpSessionId)` resumes it and only the unseen part travels.
- **Profile change** (`cfgKey`): fork of the live session with the new options, no replay.
- **System prompt change** (only when it travels: `append`/`replace`): a new session with a
  bounded replay.
- **Revert:**
  - with `smartRevert` (default on), the session is forked back to the point before the
    reverted message (`resumeSessionAt`, from the transcript checkpoint), with no replay;
  - if that isn't possible, a new session with a bounded replay.
- **Compaction:** served in the live session (see `serveCompaction`). With `historyMode: "v2"`
  the resulting `<conversation-checkpoint>` is adopted without a new session.
- **Any other divergence:** a new session with a bounded replay.

### Mode and effort per agent
Per-agent options travel like this:
1. They live in `plugins[].options.agents.<name>.options`, because V2's `Agent.Info` has no
   `options` field.
2. The `context` hook puts them in `event.options` on every call.
3. V2 nests them as `providerOptions.<providerID>`.
4. `doStream` reads them (`effectiveCtrl`).
5. `setSessionMode`/`setSessionConfigOption` apply them live.

The effort chosen as a **model variant** (`acp/default#high`) lands in the same place, through
the variant's `settings`. An explicit `effort` of the agent wins (request > model defaults).
`effort` only applies when the model exposes levels in `session/configOptions`; otherwise
it's a non-fatal warning.

### Permission bridge (native tools)
When the agent uses a **native** Claude Code tool that OpenCode can't run for it (Skill,
NotebookEdit, WebSearch, native subagents, ExitPlanMode…), Claude Code calls
`requestPermission` (ACP). The provider routes the decision:

1. **Rules first** (`evaluate` in `bridge-rules.ts`). With `ocAgent`, the native tool name
   (the first word of the ACP tool title) and its target (the skill name, the notebook path,
   the command…), it looks at the published rules and `always.json`.
   - `allow`/`deny` decide with **no dialog**.
   - `action:"*"` rules are ignored, and the default is `ask` (fail-safe).
2. **`ask` → a `question` dialog.** `onRequestPermission` returns a pending Promise and
   **emits to OpenCode** a tool call of OpenCode's own **`question`** tool
   (`{questions:[{question, header:"Permission", options:[Allow once, Always allow, Deny]}]}`),
   then `finish` (same pattern as a tool call). OpenCode runs `question` and the dialog shows
   up in the TUI.
3. **The answer.** The next `doStream` carries the `question` result.
   - `detectContinuation` tells it apart from tool results (`pendingPermissions` vs
     `pendingTools`), and `questionVerdict` parses it: the exact label of the typed output
     (`{answers:[["Always allow"]]}`), or the rendered text (`"q"="Always allow"`).
   - `Always allow` stores the rule in `always.json` (`addAlwaysRule`).
   - **Anything ambiguous fails CLOSED** (deny), including a free-form typed answer.

Robustness:
- **Cancel.** In V2, OpenCode reads each stream to the end, so a cancel is a **real abort**
  (`onCancel` → `abortTurn`).
- **Draining.** Ending a turn drains `pendingPermissions` as deny, so the agent never hangs.
  A request that arrives with the stream closed is **queued** for the next continuation.
- **Ids.** Question ids carry the session's own prefix (`<idPrefix>perm_N`).
- **No `question` tool.** If the agent lacks `question` (`hasQuestion` from the hook), the
  request is denied with a reason.
- **ExitPlanMode.** It shows the agent's real options (`askPlanApproval`); a typed answer
  rejects the plan and reaches Claude as feedback.

### Billing (subscription vs extra usage)
Anthropic classifies the session by its **system prompt**. Forwarding OpenCode's
(`append`/`replace`) makes it a third-party app, billed as *extra usage*. With `preset` (the
default) it's the official `claude_code` preset, so it counts against the **subscription**.
This was established empirically (`scripts/verify-billing.mjs`); see the billing section of
the README.

- **Real fixtures.** `test/fixtures/v2/*.jsonl` are **real** OpenCode V2 prompts, recorded with
  `ACP_RECORD=<dir>` and anonymized with `scripts/sanitize-recording.mjs`.
- **Other suites.** `plugin`, `sessions`, `fixtures` and `compat`.

A change to `history.ts` without a real fixture behind it doesn't go in: this logic has
broken several times (0.8.0, 9299af9).

**Switching `historyMode` from `shadow` to `v2`:**
1. Use OpenCode normally for a while in `shadow` (the default).
2. Look for `shadow-diff` lines in `~/.acp-model-provider/logs/acp-YYYYMMDD.log`. Each one is
   a turn where the anchor fingerprint would have decided differently.
3. If they only show cases where `v2` avoids a needless reset, set
   `claudeCode.historyMode: "v2"` (or `ACP_HISTORY_MODE=v2`).

**Smoke test in OpenCode V2** (a test project whose `opencode.json` loads the plugin by its
absolute directory path):

```bash
cd <project> && ACP_DEBUG=1 opencode run --standalone --agent claude-default -m acp/default "reply only: ok"
```

Check the log, in this order:
1. `loading plugin`;
2. `[acp-plugin] auto-registered provider 'acp' … models: …`;
3. `agents registered: claude-default, claude-auto, claude-acceptedits, claude-plan, …`;
4. `[acp-orchestrator] connected to agent`.

Notes:
- `opencode run` **without `-m` ignores the agent's `model`** and uses the global model from
  config: that's how the V2 CLI behaves.
- The bridge's `question` dialog needs the interactive TUI.

**Verification scripts** (`scripts/`, not published to npm; they need `dist/`). They run
against the real `claude-agent-acp`; `VERIFY_MODEL=haiku` makes them cheaper.

| --- | --- |

| `verify-interleave-fix.mjs` | another model's turns in between are caught up |
| `verify-stream-integrity.mjs` | tool calls, reasoning block, text not cut |

**Spikes** (without OpenCode): `.mjs` scripts inside the repo that import `../dist/...` and use
the AI SDK's `streamText` or the ACP SDK directly:

```js
import { streamText } from "ai";
import { createACPModelProvider } from "../dist/index.js";
const model = createACPModelProvider({ command: "claude-agent-acp", claudeExecutable: "…" }).languageModel("sonnet");
for await (const p of streamText({ model, prompt: "say ok", providerOptions: { acp: { mode: "bypassPermissions", effort: "low" } } }).fullStream) { /* … */ }
```

**Inspecting what the provider sends:** set `ACP_RECORD=<dir>`. Each conversation gets a JSONL
file with:
- the prompt OpenCode sent, with large payloads cut;
- the decision taken (`new` / `reuse` / `continuation` / `smart-revert` / `shadow-diff`…);
- the blocks that actually went to the agent.

Cost note: a real prompt counts against your subscription. Inspection spikes (discovery,
building config, `setSessionMode`) spend no tokens.

## 6. Extending

- **New built-in agents:** they come from the discovered modes (`modeAgentDefs()` in
  `plugin/pairing.ts`, called by `agentDefs()` in `plugin/index.ts`).
  - Each entry is `{ name, description, model, variant, options }`.
  - Users replace the whole list with a plain-object `plugins[].options.agents` (no merge
    with the built-in profile), or turn it off with `agents: false`.
  - `model` and `description` are only filled when the user hasn't set them in OpenCode's
    `agents` section.
- **New per-call parameters:** add them to `ClaudeCodeControl`.
  - Read them in `effectiveCtrl`, adding the key to its allow-list so it can come per agent.
  - If they apply at runtime, apply them in `applySessionConfig`. The available calls are
    `setSessionMode`, `setSessionConfigOption` and `unstable_setSessionModel`.
- **More model metadata:** `catalog.ts` (`buildModels`/`matchCatalog`).
- **Another ACP agent (not Claude Code):** the provider is generic ACP; the command and binary
  come from the options. The Claude-specific parts live in `claude-config.ts`.

## 7. Non-obvious design decisions

- **Common native tools disabled.**
  - What: `disallowedTools` on the built-in agents covers Bash, Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit,
    Glob, Grep, WebFetch and TodoWrite, plus `tools: []` in the clean brain.
  - Why: two executors would break "OpenCode orchestrates", and what a native tool reads never
    reaches OpenCode's history. After a switch to another model that content would be gone.
- **The MCP runtime runs with `node`, not `process.execPath`.** Inside OpenCode,
  `process.execPath` is the `opencode` binary, which doesn't run an arbitrary JS script.
  Override with `ACP_RUNTIME_NODE`.
- **Isolated config dir needs the credentials link.** An empty dir breaks auth, so
  `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is **linked** in.
- **`systemPromptMode: "preset"` by default.** Any other mode forwards OpenCode's system prompt
  and triggers *extra usage*.
- **EPIPE hardening.** When the agent closes (e.g. after an API error), sockets and pipes raise
  EPIPE. This is handled in `model.ts`, `discover.ts`, `mcp-host.ts` and `mcp-runtime.ts`.
- **The `default` model.**
  - What: `default` is Claude Code's recommended model, an Opus with a 1M context.
  - Observed: `sonnet[1m]` is billed as *extra usage*.
